rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zamakhsharī places the Quran first among divine favors because religion is the foremost favor; its revelation and teaching are the highest-ranked revelation and the summit, proof, and standard of heavenly books.
rows.anchor: وهي نعمة الدين ، فقدم من نعمة الدين ما هو في أعلى مراتبها وأقصى مراقيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning human creation after the Quran shows that humanity was created for religion and to know revelation and scripture; the purpose of human creation is presented as prior to creation.
rows.anchor: وأخر ذكر خلق الإنسان عن ذكره ، ثم أتبعه إياه : ليعلم أنه إنما خلقه للدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human eloquent, expressive speech distinguishes people from other animals by conveying what is inward.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر ما تميز به من سائر الحيوان من البيان ، وهو المنطق الفصيح المعرب عما في الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Raḥmān is the subject; the following verbs with their pronouns form successive predicates without conjunctions, matching a listing of favors and making each clause an independent rebuke to deniers.
rows.anchor: أخبار مترادفة ، وإخلاؤها من العاطف لمجيئها على نمط التعديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He illustrates the rebuke by listing how Zayd was helped after poverty, lowliness, and scarcity, then asking what kindness he could deny.
rows.anchor: زيد أغناك بعد فقر ، أعزك بعد ذل ، كثرك بعد قلة ، فعل بك ما لم يفعل أحد بأحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon move by a known, precise calculation in their orbits and stations, benefiting people, including by enabling the reckoning of years and time.
rows.anchor: بحسبان } بحساب معلوم وتقدير سوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-najm here means stemless plants that emerge from the earth, such as vegetables, while al-shajar means trees with trunks.
rows.anchor: والنبات الذي ينجم من الأرض لا ساق له كالبقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plants' prostration is their submission to God in the purpose for which He created them and their inability to resist, likened to a worshipper's obedient prostration.
rows.anchor: تشبيها بالساجد من المكلفين في انقياده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clauses about calculation and prostration connect by meaning without a verbal conjunction: the calculation belongs to God and the prostration is to Him alone.
rows.anchor: استغنى فيهما عن الوصل اللفظي بالوصل المعنوي ، لما علم أن الحسبان حسبانه ، والسجود له لا لغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first clauses omit conjunctions so each independently rebukes deniers by enumerating benefactions; conjunctions resume for clauses that suit and approach each other.
rows.anchor: ثم رد الكلام إلى منهاجه بعد التبكيت في وصل ما يجب وصله للتناسب والتقارب بالعاطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two clauses suit one another because sun and moon are celestial, plants earthly, heaven and earth are paired, and celestial calculation resembles the plants' submission.
rows.anchor: إن الشمس والقمر سماويان ، والنجم والشجر أرضيان ، فبين القبيلين تناسب من حيث التقابل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative explanation says that teaching the Quran made it a sign and a miracle.
rows.anchor: علم القرءان } جعله علامة وآية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the human created in the verse as Adam.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه : الإنسان آدم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A second report from Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the human as the Messenger Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وعنه أيضا : محمد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid takes al-najm to mean the stars of the sky, rather than stemless vegetation.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد النجم : نجوم السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God raised and made the sky firm as the source of His judgments, decrees, commands, and prohibitions, and as the dwelling of angels who bring revelation; this signals His majesty and sovereignty.
rows.anchor: خلقها مرفوعة مسموكة ، حيث جعلها منشأ أحكامه ، ومصدر قضاياه ، ومتنزل أوامره ونواهيه

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh's reading has “and He lowered the balance” in place of “and He set the balance.”
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله ( وخفض الميزان )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The balance includes every instrument for weighing or measuring quantities; God placed it on earth for judgments, transactions, and the fair treatment He enjoined in giving and taking.
rows.anchor: وأراد به كل ما توزن به الأشياء وتعرف مقاديرها من ميزان وقرسطون ومكيال ومقياس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “So that you do not transgress” can be read as a purpose clause or as an explanatory particle; ʿAbd Allāh reads “Do not transgress,” with a saying understood.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله ( لا تطغوا ) بغير أن ، على إرادة القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to weigh justly and the prohibition is against both unjust excess and short measure; repeating “the balance” strengthens the admonition and the command to use it.
rows.anchor: أمر بالتسوية ونهى عن الطغيان الذي هو اعتداء وزيادة ، وعن الخسران الذي هو تطفيف ونقصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading gives al-samāʾ in the nominative.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( والسماء ) بالرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb in “do not give short measure” has readings with fatḥa on tāʾ and with ḍamma, kasra, or fatḥa on sīn; the fatḥa analysis deletes the preposition fī from the underlying phrase.
rows.anchor: بفتح التاء وضم السين وكسرها وفتحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God lowered and spread the earth over the water.
rows.anchor: وضعها } خفضها مدحوة على الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-anām means creatures on the earth's surface; al-Ḥasan specifies humans and jinn, for whom earth is like a bed on which they move.
rows.anchor: وهو كل ما على ظهر الأرض من دابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fruits are the varied kinds of produce enjoyed for pleasure.
rows.anchor: فاكهة } ضروب مما يتفكه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-akmām are coverings such as palm fiber, fronds, and flower sheaths; all are useful, as are the date's fruit, marrow, and trunk.
rows.anchor: كل ما يكم أي يغطى من ليفة وسعفة وكفراة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation takes al-akmām as the containers around date fruit; its singular is kumm, with kasra on kāf.
rows.anchor: وقيل الأكمام أوعية التمرة الواحد كم بكسر الكاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿaṣf means crop leaves, or straw; al-rayḥān means provision and the nourishing core. Dates combine pleasure and nourishment, while grain nourishes people.
rows.anchor: ورق الزرع وقيل التبن { والريحان } الرزق وهو اللب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With kasra on al-rayḥān, the phrase means grain with its fodder leaves and the food for people; with ḍamma it means “and possessing rayḥān,” with the first noun omitted.
rows.anchor: بالكسر . ومعناه : والحب ذو العصف الذي هو علف الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes al-rayḥān as the fragrant herb; the Syrian codices read “the grain with its leaves and the rayḥān,” meaning God created or specially selected them, with an omitted noun also possible.
rows.anchor: وقيل : معناه وفيها الريحان الذي يشم ، وفي مصاحف أهل الشأم : والحب ذو العصف والريحان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual address in “which of your Lord's favors do you deny?” addresses humans and jinn, as indicated by al-anām and by the explicit dual address in 55:31.
rows.anchor: والخطاب في { ربكما تكذبان } للثقلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax expands to “why do you not return it when it reaches the throat, if you are not governed?”; the second falawlā repeats for emphasis, the pronoun refers to the soul, and “nearer to him” refers to the dying person.
rows.anchor: ترتيب الآية : فلولا ترجعونها إذا بلغت الحلقوم إن كنتم غير مدينين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayr madīnīn means not ruled or governed, from the expression for a ruler governing subjects.
rows.anchor: من دان السلطان الرعية إذا ساسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is nearer to the dying person than the gathered family through His power and knowledge, or through the angels of death.
rows.anchor: يا أهل الميت بقدرتنا وعلمنا ، أو بملائكة الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge exposes denial: people call a miraculous book magic, a messenger a liar, and rain the work of a star; if no agent takes the soul and their denial of the life-giver and raiser is true, why can they not return it to the body?
rows.anchor: فما لكم لا ترجعون الروح إلى البدن بعد بلوغه الحلقوم إن لم يكن ثم قابض وكنتم صادقين في تعطيلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the deceased belongs to the foremost group, one of the three groups named at the surah's beginning, he receives repose.
rows.anchor: من السابقين من الأزواج الثلاثة المذكورة في أول السورة

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha transmits from the Prophet a reading with ḍamma on rūḥ; al-Ḥasan also reads it this way and explains rūḥ as mercy, like life for the recipient of mercy.
rows.anchor: وروت عائشة رضي الله عنها عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : فروح ، بالضم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation gives rūḥ the sense of permanence, so the deceased receives both rest and lasting provision and bliss.
rows.anchor: وقيل : البقاء ، أي : فهذان له معا ، وهو الخلود مع الرزق والنعيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rayḥān means provision.
rows.anchor: والريحان : الرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greeting means “peace to you, companion of the right,” from your fellow people of the right who greet you, as in 56:26.
rows.anchor: أي : فسلام لك يا صاحب اليمين من إخوانك أصحاب اليمين ، أي : يسلمون عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “welcome” of boiling water echoes the description of their welcome in 56:56.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى : { هاذا نزلهم يوم الدين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lightened reading is reported for fanuzul.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالتخفيف { وتصلية جحيم } قرئت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taṣliyat jaḥīm is read in the nominative or genitive, coordinated with naẓul or ḥamīm.
rows.anchor: قرئت بالرفع والجر عطفا على نزل وحميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What this surah revealed is the fully established truth of certainty.
rows.anchor: الذي أنزل في هذه السورة

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report from the Messenger says that whoever recites Sūrat al-Wāqiʿa every night will never suffer want; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وعلى آله وسلم :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Ḥadīd is Medinan, has twenty-nine verses, and was revealed after al-Zalzala.
rows.anchor: مدنية ، وهي تسع وعشرون آية ( نزلت بعد الزلزلة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that Paradise's people and Hell's people are not equal warns people whose heedlessness, attachment to immediate desires, and neglect of consequences make them act as if they do not know the difference; they should learn that victory belongs to Paradise's people.
rows.anchor: هذا تنبيه للناس وإيذان لهم بأنهم لفرط غفلتهم وقلة فكرهم في العاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke resembles telling a disobedient son “he is your father”: it reminds him of a relationship whose rights require kindness and care.
rows.anchor: كما تقول لمن يعق أباه : هو أبوك ، تجعله بمنزلة من لا يعرفه

rows.speaker: أصحاب الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī's followers infer from the verse that a Muslim is not executed for killing a non-Muslim and that non-Muslims do not acquire Muslim property by force.
rows.anchor: وقد استدل أصحاب الشافعي رضي الله عنه بهذه الآية على أن المسلم لا يقتل بالكافر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account says the Prophet called for a bowl of water, dipped his hand in it, and the women then dipped their hands.
rows.anchor: دعا بقدح من ماء فعمس فيه يده ، ثم غمسن أيديهن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says the Prophet shook hands with the women while a qatari cloth covered his hand.
rows.anchor: صافحهن وكان على يده ثوب قطري

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third account says ʿUmar shook hands with the women on the Prophet's behalf.
rows.anchor: كان عمر يصافحهن عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An account says some poor Muslims maintained friendly ties with Jews to obtain their fruit.
rows.anchor: روي أن بعض فقراء المسلمين كانوا يواصلون اليهود ليصيبوا من ثمارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews are described as people under God's anger who lost hope of a share in the afterlife because they stubbornly opposed the Messenger despite knowing he was described in the Torah.
rows.anchor: لعنادهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ، وهم يعلمون أنه الرسول المنعوت في التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison means disbelievers despair that their dead will be raised and returned alive.
rows.anchor: من موتاهم أن يبعثوا ويرجعوا أحياء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative construal makes “the companions of the graves” explain “the disbelievers”: those buried have recognized the ugliness of their state and outcome in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: بيان للكفار ، أي : كما يئس الكفار الذين قبروا من خير الآخرة

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report from the Messenger promises that believing men and women will intercede for whoever recites Sūrat al-Mumtaḥana on Judgment Day; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Ṣaff is Medinan, has fourteen verses, and was revealed after al-Taghābun.
rows.anchor: مدنية ، وآياتها 14 ( نزلت بعد التغابن )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The test asks which people are best in intellect, most careful about God's prohibitions, and quickest to obey Him.
rows.anchor: أيكم أحسن عقلا وأورع عن محارم الله وأسرع في طاعة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Life enables people to act, while death urges them to choose good over evil because resurrection and recompense necessarily follow; death is mentioned first because keeping it before one's eyes most strongly motivates action.
rows.anchor: سلط علكم الموت الذي هو داعيكم إلى اختيار العمل الحسن على القبيح ، لأن وراءه البعث والجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAzīz means overpowering and beyond the reach of those who do evil; al-Ghafūr forgives wrongdoers who repent.
rows.anchor: العزيز } الغالب الذي لا يعجزه من أساء العمل { الغفور } لمن تاب من أهل الإساءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭibāqan means heaven upon heaven, fitted layer upon layer; grammatically it can be a verbal noun, an ellipsis for “having layers,” or a passive construction.
rows.anchor: طباقا } مطابقة بعضها فوق بعض ، من طابق النعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The variant tafawut/tafawut has the same meaning: no discord or imbalance in creation; mismatch is when one part fails to suit another, and the opposite is mutual proportion.
rows.anchor: من تفاوت } وقرىء : ( من تفوت ) ، ومعنى البناءين واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The no-discord clause qualifies the layered heavens; replacing “in them” with “in the creation of the All-Merciful” magnifies their creation and signals that their harmony comes from His power.
rows.anchor: فوضع مكان الضمير قوله : { خلق الرحمان } تعظيما لخلقهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent choice between speaking privately and publicly means both are equally known to God; He knows the heart's contents before tongues express them, so He certainly knows spoken words.
rows.anchor: ظاهره الأمر بأحد الأمرين : الإسرار والإجهار . ومعناه : ليستو عندكم إسراركم وإجهاركم في علم الله بهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question whether the Creator knows His creation is answered by God's being subtle and fully aware, whose knowledge reaches what is outward and hidden.
rows.anchor: من خلاق } منصوبا بمعنى : ألا يعلم مخلوقه وهذه حاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the polytheists discussed matters privately and told one another to hide their speech so Muhammad's God could not hear; God exposed their ignorance by informing His Messenger of their talk.
rows.anchor: وروى أن المشركين كانوا يتكلمون فيما بينهم بأشياء ، فيظهر الله رسوله علتها ، فيقولون : أسروا قولكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects reading the question as simply “could one who creates fail to know?” because “while He is subtle and aware” is a circumstantial qualifier; the question must concern a specific object while God knows everything.
rows.anchor: ألا يعلم كذا وهو عالم بكل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Walking on earth's shoulders is an image of extreme subjugation: a camel's shoulders and hump are too delicate and prominent for a rider to tread on, so land made walkable even there is wholly subdued.
rows.anchor: لأن المنكبين وملتقاهما من الغارب أرق شيء من البعير وأنباه عن أن يطأه الراكب بقدمه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the earth's shoulders to mean its mountains.
rows.anchor: وقيل : مناكبها جبالها

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the phrase as making travel through the mountains easy; if even mountain travel is possible, the earth is all the more thoroughly subdued.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : معناه سهل لكم السلوك في جبالها ، فإذا أمكنكم السلوك في جبالها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further explanation takes the earth's shoulders to mean its sides.
rows.anchor: وقيل : جوانبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “To Him is the resurrection” means people will be raised to Him, who will question them about gratitude for His blessings.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : وإليه نشوركم ، فهو مسائلكم عن شكر ما أنعم به عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Who is in heaven” can mean God's sovereign realm in heaven, the abode of angels and location of the throne, seat, and preserved tablet from which decrees and commands descend.
rows.anchor: من ملكوته في السماء ؛ لأنها مسكن ملائكته وثم عرشه وكرسيه واللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the address follows the polytheists' belief that God is in heaven and that mercy and punishment descend from Him, while affirming that He transcends place.
rows.anchor: يعتقدون التشبيه ، وأنه في السماء ، وأن الرحمة والعذاب ينزلان منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke speaks according to the anthropomorphists' own belief, as one might warn an anthropomorphist sinning that the One above the Throne could punish him.
rows.anchor: فقيل لهم على حسب اعتقادهم : أأمنتم من تزعمون أنه في السماء ، وهو متعال عن المكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb “you will know” has both second-person and third-person readings.
rows.anchor: قرىء : بالتاء والياء { كيف نذير } أي إذا رأيتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the threatened event is seen, people will understand the warning, but that knowledge will come too late to help.
rows.anchor: أي إذا رأيتم المنذر به علمتم كيف إنذاري حين لا ينفعكم العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣāffāt describes birds spreading and aligning their leading feathers in the air; yaqbiḍna describes folding their wings as they beat their flanks.
rows.anchor: صافات } باسطات أجنحتهن في الجو عند طيرانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text uses a verb for folding rather than an active participle because spreading wings is the natural, primary flight position, like extending limbs in swimming; folding is a temporary aid to movement.
rows.anchor: لأن الأصل في الطيران هو صف الأجنحة ؛ لأن الطيران في الهواء كالسباحة في الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The All-Merciful alone keeps birds aloft by power, the arrangement of their leading and tail feathers, and the bodily shape and properties that enable flight.
rows.anchor: بقدرته وبما دبر لهن من القوادم والخوافي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's being all-seeing means He knows how to create and manage wondrous things.
rows.anchor: يعلم كيف يخلق وكيف يدبر العجائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects treating akabba as a regular intransitive passive of kabba: this is an anomalous analysis, and no afʿala pattern is a regular passive; the regular intransitive is inkabba.
rows.anchor: يقال : كببته فأكب ، من الغرائب والشواذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rather, akabba belongs with forms such as infaḍḍa and alʾama: it means entering a state and becoming bent over; qashʿa/aqshaʿ works similarly, while the passive forms are inkabba and inqashaʿa.
rows.anchor: ومعناه : دخل في الكب ، وصار ذا كب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bent-over person walks awkwardly over uneven familiar ground and repeatedly falls on his face, unlike someone walking upright without falling; alternatively, he deviates from a straight path.
rows.anchor: يمشي معتسفا في مكان معتاد غير مستو فيه انخفاض وارتفاع ، فيعثر كل ساعة فيخر على وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation contrasts a blind person groping off course and repeatedly falling with a sound-sighted person walking straight on a guided path; the comparison represents believer and unbeliever.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد الأعمى الذي لا يهتدي إلى الطريق فيعتسف ، فلا يزال ينكب على وجهه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the unbeliever bent over God's disobedience and will therefore be gathered face-down on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة : الكافر أكب على معاصي الله تعالى فحشره الله يوم القيامة على وجهه

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī identifies the bent-over person as Abū Jahl and the upright walker as the Messenger; another report names Ḥamza as the upright person.
rows.anchor: وعن الكلبي : عني به أبو جهل بن هشام . وبالسوي : رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ، وقيل : حمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Your Lord knows best” can mean He knows the truly mad, who strayed from His path, and the rational, guided people; alternatively, it promises or threatens that He knows each group's recompense.
rows.anchor: بالمجانين على الحقيقة ، وهم الذين ضلوا عن سبيله { وهو أعلم } بالعقلاء وهم المهتدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command not to obey the deniers incites firm resistance; they had tried to persuade the Prophet to worship God for a time and their idols for a time in return for leaving him unharmed.
rows.anchor: وكانوا قد أرادوه على أن يعبد الله مدة ، وآلهتهم مدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tudhinu means to soften, accommodate, or compromise, and fa-yudhinūn means that they would then compromise.
rows.anchor: لو تلين وتصانع { فيدهنون } فإن قلت : لم رفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The raised fa-yudhinūn is not subjunctive as a response to the wish; the construction instead predicates a deleted subject, “then they would compromise,” or says they compromise now in hope of his accommodation.
rows.anchor: وهو أن جعل خبر مبتدأ محذوف ، أي : فهم يدهنون

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh reports that Hārūn said some codices have the variant “they wished you to compromise, so they would compromise.”
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه : وزعم هرون أنها في بعض المصاحف ودوا لو تدهن فيدهنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sāʾala incorporates the meaning of daʿā and takes its construction: it is as if a caller invoked punishment, as in the expression “invoke something” and the verse about people calling for every fruit in 43:73.
rows.anchor: معنى دعا ، فعدى تعديته ، كأنه قيل : دعا داع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the speaker was al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, who challenged God to send stones or painful punishment if the message was true.
rows.anchor: هو النضر بن الحرث قال : إن كان هذا هو الحق من عندك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the speaker as the Messenger, who sought to hasten punishment for the unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ، استعجل بعذاب للكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading sāla sāʾil can derive from asking in Quraysh dialect, where they say salta tasʾalu; alternatively it derives from flowing.
rows.anchor: من السؤال وهي لغة قريش ، يقولون : سلت تسأل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās's reading sāla sayl supports derivation from flowing; sayl is a verbal noun used like the active participle ghāʾir, so punishment surged over and destroyed them.
rows.anchor: والسيل : مصدر في معنى السائل ، كالغور بمعنى الغائر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the question was about whom God's punishment descends on and whom it strikes; on this reading, sāʾala means to ask about or be concerned with.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة : سأل سائل عن عذاب الله على من ينزل وبمن يقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the first interpretation, li-l-kāfirīn can modify the punishment as its description, the verb as its object, or wāqiʿ as a description meaning punishment descending for them; for the second it is a standalone answer that the punishment is for unbelievers.
rows.anchor: متصل بعذاب صفة له ، أي : بعذاب واقع كائن للكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min Allāh can modify wāqiʿ, meaning coming from God, or dāfiʿ, meaning no one can avert it when its appointed time and wisdom arrive.
rows.anchor: واقع من عنده ، أو بدافع ؛ بمعنى : ليس له دافع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhī al-maʿārij means possessor of ascents or stairways, from the plural maʿraj; they are then described as distant in height.
rows.anchor: ذي المصاعد جمع معرج ، ثم وصف المصاعد وبعد مداها في العلو والارتفاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels and Spirit ascend to God's throne and to where His commands descend; the Spirit is Gabriel, singled out for his virtue.
rows.anchor: جبريل عليه السلام ، أفرده لتميزه بفضله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the Spirit is a created being who guards the angels, just as angels guard people.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الروح خلق هم حفظة على الملائكة ، كما أن الملائكة حفظة على الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time in which the angels ascend is equivalent to fifty thousand years by human reckoning.
rows.anchor: كمقدار مدة { خمسين ألف سنة } مما يعد الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “So be patient” connects to the one asking for punishment: the mocking demand and denial of revelation distressed the Prophet, so he was told to endure it; the hostile question about its target likewise came from Meccan unbelievers.
rows.anchor: لأن استعجال النصر بالعذاب إنما كان على وجه الاستهزاء برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والتكذيب بالوحي
